claims.text: RBAC decides what a caller may do from the roles assigned to it, instead of granting permissions to each user individually.
claims.source_hint: NIST RBAC model (INCITS 359); glossary entry rbac

claims.text: The donhang realm defines realm roles customer and staff; the five customers have customer and the staff account (lan.do@example.com) has staff.
A protocol mapper (oidc-usermodel-realm-role-mapper) on the donhang-app client writes the user's realm roles into a multivalued claim named roles, in the access token only (id.token.claim false).
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-2: keycloak/donhang-realm.json:46-59; Keycloak Server Admin Guide: protocol mappers, User Realm Role mapper

claims.text: Keycloak evaluates the user's roles each time it issues an access token; a role granted or removed later does not change tokens already issued.
claims.source_hint: Keycloak Server Admin Guide: protocol mappers / role mappings (applied at token creation); RFC 7519 (a signed JWT cannot change after signing)

claims.text: DonHang.Api reads roles from the validated token's claims and does not call Keycloak to look them up (local JwtBearer validation; no introspection or userinfo call).

TokenValidationParameters.RoleClaimType names the claim type whose values ASP.NET Core treats as the user's roles (ClaimsIdentity.RoleClaimType, used by IsInRole and RequireRole); Program.cs sets it to roles, with MapInboundClaims = false keeping the name roles.
claims.source_hint: API docs: TokenValidationParameters.RoleClaimType; JwtBearerOptions.MapInboundClaims; ClaimsPrincipal.IsInRole; Program.cs:54-55

claims.text: options.AddPolicy("StaffOnly", policy => policy.RequireRole("staff")) defines a policy that succeeds only when the user is in role staff; [Authorize(Policy = "StaffOnly")] applies it to the Ship action.
claims.source_hint: ASP.NET Core docs: Role-based authorization (policy-based role checks, RequireRole); Policy-based authorization; Program.cs:64, OrdersController.cs:91

claims.text: On an endpoint with [Authorize(Policy=...)], a request with no valid token is challenged (401 with JwtBearer), and an authenticated caller who fails the policy is forbidden (403), before the action runs.
claims.source_hint: ASP.NET Core docs: Authorize with a specific scheme / challenge vs forbid; outputs/stage-2/scripts/backend/staff-only.txt (401, 403)

claims.text: staff-only.sh output: customer 1's token has roles ["customer"], the staff token ["staff"]; PATCH /api/v1/orders/1/ship answers 401 with no token, 403 as customer 1 (owner of order 1), 200 with status shipped as staff.
staff-only.sh sets order 1 to paid, gets access tokens for customer 1 and the staff account, and sends the ship request three times (no token, customer, staff).

The realm issues access tokens for 300 s (accessTokenLifespan 300, token response expires_in 300); with JwtBearer's default clock skew (5 min, unchanged in Program.cs) a removed role can keep working for minutes.

A scope is requested for the client when the flow starts (Keycloak may add default client scopes); roles are assigned to the user and reach the token via the client mapper whatever scopes are requested; oauth-code-flow.sh asks for openid, response scope is "email openid profile".
claims.source_hint: RFC 6749 §3.3; donhang-realm.json:32-59 (defaultClientScopes, role mapper on client); scripts/backend/oauth-code-flow.sh + outputs/stage-2/scripts/backend/oauth-code-flow.txt

claims.text: The Ship action contains no role check; OrderService.ShipOrderAsync calls Order.Ship(), which decides whether the order can be shipped; the policy check on the endpoint applies to any client sending the request.
An ownership check alone cannot restrict shipping, because customer 1 owns order 1 and must still be refused; a rule for a whole group of users fits a role.
claims.source_hint: reasoning from the design; staff-only.sh output (403 for the owner)

claims.text: [Authorize] with no policy or roles requires only an authenticated user, so any caller with a valid token passes it.

With JwtBearerOptions.MapInboundClaims = true (the default) incoming JWT claim types such as sub are mapped to longer ClaimTypes URIs (sub -> ClaimTypes.NameIdentifier); false keeps the names from the token.
claims.source_hint: API docs: JwtBearerOptions.MapInboundClaims; JwtSecurityTokenHandler.DefaultInboundClaimTypeMap; refs blazor-web-app-with-oidc.md (MapInboundClaims false)
